```{r schematic-setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.4, fig.retina = 2, out.width = "100%"
)

library("naboer")
library("tibble")

have_ggplot <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
have_sf <- have_ggplot && requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE)
have_ape <- have_ggplot && requireNamespace("ape", quietly = TRUE)
if (have_ggplot) library("ggplot2")

fold_points <- function(folds, selected, panels) {
  observations <- as_tibble(fold_data(folds))
  assessment <- assessment_indices(folds, folds = selected)
  omission <- omission_indices(folds, folds = selected)

  pieces <- lapply(seq_along(selected), function(i) {
    role <- rep("analysis", nrow(observations))
    role[omission[[i]]] <- "omitted"
    role[assessment[[i]]] <- "assessment"
    add_column(observations,
      observation = seq_len(nrow(observations)),
      panel = factor(panels[i], levels = panels),
      role = factor(role, levels = c("analysis", "omitted", "assessment"))
    )
  })
  dplyr::bind_rows(pieces)
}

fold_scales <- function() {
  role_labels <- c(
    analysis = "Used to fit", omitted = "Left out only",
    assessment = "Prediction scored"
  )
  labels <- function(roles) unname(role_labels[roles])
  list(
    scale_colour_manual(NULL,
      values = c(analysis = "#737373", omitted = "#B45F06", assessment = "#0072B2"),
      labels = labels
    ),
    scale_shape_manual(NULL,
      values = c(analysis = 16, omitted = 18, assessment = 15),
      labels = labels
    ),
    theme_minimal(base_size = 11),
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", margin = margin(b = 6))
    )
  )
}
```

Every fold defines which observations are used to fit the model and whose
predictions are scored. The **analysis** rows are used for fitting. The
**assessment** rows are used for scoring. The **omission** set contains all the
rows left out of fitting, including the assessment rows and any extra exclusions.
In the figures, grey circles mark analysis rows, blue squares mark assessment
rows and orange diamonds mark the extra exclusions. Each panel shows membership
for the labelled fold or design.

The spatial and spatiotemporal examples use `sf`. The tree example uses `ape`.

```{r schematic-dependencies, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
if (!have_ggplot) {
  cat("Install ggplot2 to draw the figures in this vignette.\n")
}
```

## What `nei` tells mgcv

Make eight observations and specify two folds with `custom_folds()`. Fold 1
scores the prediction for row 3. Fold 2 scores rows 4 and 5. Rows 3 and 4 are
left out of fitting in both folds, and each is scored in a different fold.

```{r nei-schematic-data}
observations <- tibble(time = 1:8)
folds <- custom_folds(observations,
  assessment = list(3L, 4:5),
  omission = list(2:4, 3:6)
)
```

```{r nei-membership-schematic, eval=have_ggplot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=2.35, fig.alt="Two folds over eight data rows. Fold 1 fits rows 1 and 5 through 8, leaves out rows 2 and 4 without scoring, and scores row 3. Fold 2 fits rows 1, 2, 7 and 8, leaves out rows 3 and 6 without scoring, and scores rows 4 and 5."}
fold_points(folds, 1:2, c("Fold 1", "Fold 2")) |>
  ggplot(aes(observation, panel, colour = role, shape = role)) +
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  fold_scales() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:8, expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev, expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  labs(x = "Row of fold_data(folds)", y = NULL)
```

`as_nei()` packs the rows left out of fitting into `a` and the rows scored into
`d`, one fold after another. In each vector the numbers **inside the boxes** are
row numbers in `fold_data(folds)`. The numbers on the horizontal axis are
**positions in the packed vectors**. `ma` and `md` give the last position for
each fold in `a` and `d`, respectively. Each fold starts one position after the
previous endpoint, with the first fold starting at position 1.

```{r nei-schematic-export}
nei <- as_nei(folds, data = fold_data(folds))
```

```{r nei-packing-schematic, eval=have_ggplot, echo=FALSE, fig.height=3.1, fig.alt="An omission strip a contains rows 2, 3, 4 for fold 1 and rows 3, 4, 5, 6 for fold 2. Its cumulative endpoints ma are 3 and 7. An assessment strip d contains row 3 for fold 1 and rows 4 and 5 for fold 2. Its cumulative endpoints md are 1 and 3."}
packed_rows <- rbind(
  tibble(position = seq_along(nei$a), row = nei$a, track = 2),
  tibble(position = seq_along(nei$d), row = nei$d, track = 1)
)
fold_endpoints <- function(ends, pointer, track) {
  fold_number <- seq_along(ends)
  tibble(start = c(1L, head(ends, -1L) + 1L), end = ends, track = track,
    fold = paste("Fold", fold_number),
    endpoint = paste0(pointer, "[", fold_number, "] = ", ends)
  )
}
packed_folds <- rbind(
  fold_endpoints(nei$ma, "ma", 2),
  fold_endpoints(nei$md, "md", 1)
)

ggplot(packed_rows, aes(position, track)) +
  geom_tile(width = 0.9, height = 0.27, fill = "#EDF1F4") +
  geom_text(aes(label = row), size = 3.8) +
  geom_segment(data = packed_folds, inherit.aes = FALSE,
    aes(x = end, xend = end, y = track + 0.14, yend = track + 0.25),
    colour = "#526674"
  ) +
  geom_text(data = packed_folds, inherit.aes = FALSE,
    aes(end, track + 0.36, label = endpoint), size = 3.5
  ) +
  geom_segment(data = packed_folds, inherit.aes = FALSE,
    aes(x = start - 0.41, xend = end + 0.41, y = track - 0.19, yend = track - 0.19),
    colour = "#526674"
  ) +
  geom_text(data = packed_folds, inherit.aes = FALSE,
    aes((start + end) / 2, track - 0.3, label = fold), size = 3.3
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(nei$a), expand = expansion(add = 0.65)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:2, labels = c("Scored rows (d)", "Omitted rows (a)"),
    limits = c(0.57, 2.52), expand = expansion(mult = 0)
  ) +
  labs(x = "Position in packed vector", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_line(colour = "grey75"))
```

For a given set of smoothing parameters, the NCV criterion uses predictions
from the fit with each fold's `a` rows left out. It adds the loss for the
corresponding `d` rows, here row 3 from the first fold and rows 4 and 5 from
the second. mgcv calculates the leave-out predictions through an approximation
to refitting, chooses the smoothing parameters by minimising the criterion, and
uses all the data for the final model. See
[Assessment, omission and prediction targets](naboer.html) for a worked fit.

Use `custom_folds()` to supply membership directly or `from_rset()` to import
existing `rsample` splits. In an imported split, rows outside both the analysis
and assessment sets are the extra omissions.

## Leave-one-out and random V-fold

Both designs score every observation once across the full set of folds.
`loo_folds()` holds out one observation at a time. `vfold_folds()` assigns
observations to V folds and holds out one fold at a time. In this example the
random design has three folds, each with four observations.

```{r schematic-basic, eval=have_ggplot, fig.width=7, fig.height=2.2, fig.alt="Two rows of twelve observations. Leave-one-out assesses only observation 5. Random three-fold assesses four observations scattered along the row. All remaining observations are used for fitting."}
times <- tibble(day = 1:12, date = as.Date("2024-01-01") + day - 1L)
loo <- loo_folds(times)
random <- vfold_folds(times, v = 3, seed = 2026)

plot_fold_rows <- function(points, x_label) {
  ggplot(points, aes(x = observation, y = panel)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = panel), colour = "grey85", linewidth = 0.4) +
    geom_point(aes(colour = role, shape = role), size = 3) +
    fold_scales() +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = sort(unique(points$observation))) +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev, expand = expansion(add = c(0.35, 0.72))) +
    labs(x = x_label, y = NULL) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
}

basic_points <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fold_points(loo, 5L, "Leave-one-out"),
  fold_points(random, 1L, "Random three-fold")
)
plot_fold_rows(basic_points, "Observation")
```

## Temporal neighbourhoods and blocks

Both examples leave out days 4 to 6 and use observations on either side for
fitting. The neighbourhood has a one-day radius and scores only the focal day,
day 5. The three-day temporal block scores all three held-out days.

```{r schematic-temporal, eval=have_ggplot, fig.width=7, fig.height=2.2, fig.alt="Two timelines both leave out days 4 to 6. The neighbourhood assesses day 5 and omits days 4 and 6 without assessing them. The block assesses all three days. Earlier and later days are used for fitting in both timelines."}
time_neighbours <- neighbourhoods(times,
  index = date, temporal = temporal_window(time_span(1, "days"))
)
time_blocks <- temporal_folds(times, index = date, size = time_span(3, "days"))

time_points <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fold_points(time_neighbours, 5L, "Focal neighbourhood"),
  fold_points(time_blocks, 2L, "Contiguous block")
)
plot_fold_rows(time_points, "Day")
```

## Expanding and sliding forecasts

At the origin on day 6, the expanding window uses all observations through
that day, and the sliding window uses the most recent three days. Both skip
day 7 as a gap and score forecasts for days 8 and 9, the two-day horizon.
Days 10 to 12 are beyond that horizon and unavailable for fitting at this
origin. Moving the origin forward also moves the gap and horizon.

```{r schematic-forecast, eval=have_ggplot, fig.width=7, fig.height=2.4, fig.alt="Both forecast folds have their origin on day 6, omit day 7 as a gap, assess days 8 and 9, and omit days 10 to 12 beyond the horizon. The expanding window fits days 1 to 6. The sliding window fits days 4 to 6 and omits days 1 to 3."}
origins <- times$date[c(6, 8)]
gap <- time_span(1, "days")
horizon <- time_span(2, "days")
expanding <- forecast_folds(times,
  index = date, origins = origins, gap = gap, horizon = horizon
)
sliding <- forecast_folds(times,
  index = date, origins = origins, gap = gap, horizon = horizon,
  window = "sliding", lookback = time_span(3, "days")
)

forecast_points <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fold_points(expanding, 1L, "Expanding window"),
  fold_points(sliding, 1L, "Sliding window")
)
plot_fold_rows(forecast_points, "Day") +
  annotate("segment", x = 6, xend = 6, y = 2.13, yend = 2.36,
    colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = c(6, 7, 8.5, 11), y = 2.53,
    label = c("Origin", "Gap", "Horizon", "Beyond horizon"), size = 3.1
  )
```

## Spatial holdouts and buffers

A spatial block fold scores all observations in a held-out region. Adding a
buffer leaves the assessment rows unchanged and removes nearby observations
from fitting. Here the circles mark the 120 m windows around assessment sites.
A focal spatial neighbourhood instead scores one observation per fold.

```{r schematic-spatial-designs, eval=have_sf}
sites <- tibble(
  site = LETTERS[1:12],
  easting = c(130, 250, 360, 430, 550, 720, 110, 250, 370, 450, 590, 730),
  northing = c(145, 340, 360, 350, 190, 80, 580, 710, 450, 460, 690, 550)
) |>
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("easting", "northing"), crs = 32631, remove = FALSE)

block_width <- 400
radius <- 120
site_window <- spatial_window(units::set_units(radius, "m"))
spatial_blocks <- spatial_folds(sites,
  size = units::set_units(block_width, "m"), origin = c(0, 0)
)
spatial_buffer <- buffer_folds(spatial_blocks, spatial = site_window)
spatial_focal <- neighbourhoods(sites, spatial = site_window)
```

```{r schematic-spatial-plot, eval=have_sf, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.4, fig.alt="Three maps of the same sites. A square block fold scores three sites in its lower left cell. Buffering the block adds omitted sites across its boundaries. The focal neighbourhood scores one site and omits only its nearby sites."}
spatial_panels <- c("Spatial block", "Buffered spatial block", "Focal spatial window")
spatial_points <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fold_points(spatial_blocks, 1L, spatial_panels[1]),
  fold_points(spatial_buffer, 1L, spatial_panels[2]),
  fold_points(spatial_focal, 3L, spatial_panels[3])
)
spatial_points$panel <- factor(spatial_points$panel, levels = spatial_panels)

cells <- expand.grid(
  panel = factor(spatial_panels[1:2], levels = spatial_panels),
  xmin = c(0, block_width), ymin = c(0, block_width)
)
circle_centres <- spatial_points[
  spatial_points$panel %in% spatial_panels[2:3] &
    spatial_points$role == "assessment",
]
theta <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 81)
circles <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(circle_centres)), function(i) {
  centre <- circle_centres[i, ]
  tibble(
    panel = centre$panel, site = centre$site,
    easting = centre$easting + radius * cos(theta),
    northing = centre$northing + radius * sin(theta)
  )
}))

ggplot(spatial_points, aes(easting, northing)) +
  geom_rect(
    data = cells,
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmin + block_width,
        ymin = ymin, ymax = ymin + block_width),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = NA, colour = "#95A1AC", linewidth = 0.45
  ) +
  geom_path(
    data = circles, aes(group = site),
    colour = "#9A722F", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = role, shape = role), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(vars(panel), nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 400, 800)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, 400, 800)) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(0, 800), ylim = c(0, 800), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Easting (m)", y = "Northing (m)") +
  fold_scales() +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(1.4, "lines"))
```

## Spatiotemporal neighbourhoods

Every point represents one observation at a station on a day. Both folds score
station B on day 5. The spatial window reaches 140 m either side of B and the
time window reaches one day either side of the focal date. With intersection,
observations must be inside both windows to be omitted. With union, being
inside either window is enough.

```{r schematic-joint-designs, eval=have_sf}
stations <- tibble(
  station = LETTERS[1:5],
  easting = c(75, 200, 350, 520, 685),
  northing = 100
)
station_days <- merge(stations, data.frame(day = 1:9))
# Times are elapsed seconds. The observations fall at the middle of each day.
station_days$time <- 86400 * (station_days$day - 0.5)
station_days <- sf::st_as_sf(station_days,
  coords = c("easting", "northing"), crs = 32631, remove = FALSE
)
focal_row <- which(station_days$station == "B" & station_days$day == 5L)

station_radius <- 140
station_window <- spatial_window(units::set_units(station_radius, "m"))
day_window <- temporal_window(time_span(1, "days"))
near_in_both <- neighbourhoods(station_days,
  spatial = station_window, temporal = day_window,
  key = station, index = time, combine = "intersection"
)
near_in_either <- neighbourhoods(station_days,
  spatial = station_window, temporal = day_window,
  key = station, index = time, combine = "union"
)
```

```{r schematic-joint-plot, eval=have_sf, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=3.4, fig.alt="Two station-by-day grids. Both score station B on day five. In the intersection panel, omissions fall in the overlap of the near-station and near-date bands. In the union panel, omissions extend across both bands."}
window_panels <- c("Intersection", "Union")
window_points <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  fold_points(near_in_both, focal_row, window_panels[1]),
  fold_points(near_in_either, focal_row, window_panels[2])
)
window_points$panel <- factor(window_points$panel, levels = window_panels)

centre <- station_days[focal_row, ]
window_extent <- tibble(
  panel = factor(c("Intersection", "Union", "Union"), levels = window_panels),
  xmin = c(centre$day - 1, centre$day - 1, 0.5),
  xmax = c(centre$day + 1, centre$day + 1, 9.5),
  ymin = c(centre$easting - station_radius, 0, centre$easting - station_radius),
  ymax = c(centre$easting + station_radius, 800, centre$easting + station_radius)
)

ggplot(window_points, aes(day, easting)) +
  geom_rect(
    data = window_extent,
    aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "#E4ECF1"
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = role, shape = role), size = 2.8) +
  facet_wrap(vars(panel), nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:9, limits = c(0.5, 9.5), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = stations$easting, labels = stations$station,
    limits = c(0, 800), expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(x = "Day", y = "Station (ordered by easting)") +
  fold_scales()
```

## Spatiotemporal blocks

For the same stations and dates, use 400 m spatial blocks and three-day time
blocks. The crossed design holds out one spatial block during one time block.
The space-only design holds out a spatial block across all dates. The time-only
design holds out a time block across all stations. Each panel shows the fold
that includes station B on day 5.

```{r schematic-crossed-designs, eval=have_sf}
block_modes <- c(
  crossed = "Crossed space and time",
  space = "Space only",
  time = "Time only"
)
block_points <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(block_modes), function(mode) {
  design <- spatiotemporal_folds(station_days,
    spatial_size = units::set_units(block_width, "m"),
    temporal_size = time_span(3, "days"),
    spatial_origin = c(0, 0), temporal_origin = 0,
    mode = mode, key = station, index = time
  )
  has_focal_row <- vapply(assessment_indices(design), function(rows) {
    focal_row %in% rows
  }, logical(1))
  fold_points(design, which(has_focal_row), block_modes[[mode]])
}))
block_points$panel <- factor(block_points$panel, levels = block_modes)
```

```{r schematic-crossed-plot, eval=have_sf, fig.width=8, fig.height=3.4, fig.alt="Three station-by-day grids. Crossed blocks hold out stations A to C on days four to six. Space-only blocks hold out those stations on every day. Time-only blocks hold out those days at all stations."}
space_boundaries <- tibble(
  panel = factor(block_modes[c("crossed", "space")], levels = block_modes),
  boundary = block_width
)
time_boundaries <- expand.grid(
  panel = factor(block_modes[c("crossed", "time")], levels = block_modes),
  boundary = c(3.5, 6.5)
)

ggplot(block_points, aes(day, easting)) +
  geom_hline(
    data = space_boundaries, aes(yintercept = boundary),
    colour = "#95A1AC", linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    data = time_boundaries, aes(xintercept = boundary),
    colour = "#95A1AC", linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = role, shape = role), size = 2.7) +
  facet_wrap(vars(panel), nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 3, 5, 7, 9), limits = c(0.5, 9.5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = stations$easting, labels = stations$station, limits = c(0, 800)
  ) +
  labs(x = "Day", y = "Station (ordered by easting)") +
  fold_scales()
```

## Observational groups

Use `group_folds()` to score every observation from one site together. For
nested groups, select all the columns that identify a group. Supply `v` to
allocate whole groups to a smaller number of folds.

```{r schematic-groups, eval=have_ggplot, fig.width=7, fig.height=3, fig.alt="Two folds shown as sets of four visits to each of three sites. The first fold assesses all visits to site A and the second assesses all visits to site B. Each fold fits on visits to the other two sites."}
visits <- tibble(
  site = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 4),
  visit = rep(1:4, times = 3)
)
site_folds <- group_folds(visits, group = site)

fold_points(site_folds, 1:2, c("Hold out site A", "Hold out site B")) |>
  ggplot(aes(visit, site)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = site), colour = "grey82") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = role, shape = role), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(vars(panel)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:4) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = c("C", "B", "A")) +
  labs(x = "Visit", y = "Site") +
  fold_scales()
```

## Environmental clusters

`environmental_folds()` can cluster observations by numeric predictors using
k-means. Each cluster becomes a holdout. Use `strata` to hold out existing
environmental categories such as habitat types.

```{r schematic-environments, eval=have_ggplot, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.5, fig.alt="Temperature and moisture scatterplots with three separated clusters. One fold assesses all four observations in the cool, wet cluster. Another assesses the four warmest observations. Each fold fits on the remaining two clusters."}
climate <- tibble(
  temperature = c(10, 11, 12, 10.5, 15, 16, 17, 16.5, 22, 23, 25, 24),
  moisture = c(72, 77, 70, 65, 35, 43, 38, 31, 49, 57, 53, 45)
)
climate_folds <- environmental_folds(
  climate, predictors = c(temperature, moisture), v = 3, seed = 22
)
climate_groups <- assessment_indices(climate_folds)
cluster_temperature <- vapply(climate_groups, function(rows) {
  mean(climate$temperature[rows])
}, numeric(1))
selected_clusters <- c(which.min(cluster_temperature), which.max(cluster_temperature))
outlines <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(climate_groups), function(i) {
  points <- climate[climate_groups[[i]], ]
  hull <- grDevices::chull(points$temperature, points$moisture)
  transform(points[hull, ], cluster = i)
}))

fold_points(climate_folds, selected_clusters, c("Hold out cool, wet sites", "Hold out warm sites")) |>
  ggplot(aes(temperature, moisture)) +
  geom_polygon(
    aes(group = cluster), data = outlines, fill = NA, colour = "grey82"
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = role, shape = role), size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(vars(panel)) +
  labs(x = "Temperature (°C)", y = "Soil moisture (%)") +
  fold_scales()
```

## Phylogenetic clades and neighbourhoods

A clade fold scores all observations of its held-out taxa. A focal
neighbourhood scores one observation and excludes other observations within
the specified branch-length distance. Here oak and beech are two units
apart. Both are omitted from the fold fit in each panel.

```{r schematic-phylogeny, eval=have_ape, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.4, fig.alt="Two copies of a tree with oak and beech on one branch and pine and fir on the other. The clade fold assesses oak and beech. The focal fold assesses oak and omits beech without scoring it. Both folds fit on pine and fir."}
tree <- ape::read.tree(text = "((oak:1,beech:1):2,(pine:1,fir:1):2);")
taxa <- tibble(taxon = tree$tip.label, tip_y = 4:1)
clade_folds <- phylogenetic_folds(
  taxa, tree, taxon, clades = list(c("oak", "beech"), c("pine", "fir"))
)
near_taxon <- neighbourhoods(
  taxa, phylogenetic = phylogenetic_window(tree, taxon, radius = 2)
)

tip_panels <- c("Clade holdout", "Focal oak neighbourhood")
tips <- rbind(
  fold_points(clade_folds, 1, tip_panels[1]),
  fold_points(near_taxon, 1, tip_panels[2])
)
tips$panel <- factor(tips$panel, levels = tip_panels)

depth <- ape::node.depth.edgelength(tree)
node_y <- c(taxa$tip_y, 2.5, 3.5, 1.5)
branches <- tibble(
  parent = tree$edge[, 1],
  child = tree$edge[, 2],
  x = depth[parent], xend = depth[child],
  y = node_y[child], parent_y = node_y[parent]
)
tips$depth <- depth[tips$observation]

ggplot(tips, aes(depth, tip_y)) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y),
    data = branches, inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey55"
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = x, xend = x, y = parent_y, yend = y),
    data = branches, inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey55"
  ) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = role, shape = role), size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = taxon), nudge_x = 0.14, hjust = 0, size = 3.5) +
  facet_wrap(vars(panel)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:3, expand = expansion(add = c(0.1, 0.8))) +
  labs(x = "Branch length from root", y = NULL) +
  fold_scales() +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  )
```

`phylogenetic_folds()` can also hold out groups formed by complete-linkage
clustering of distances along the tree. Use `v` for a number of clusters or
`height` for the maximum allowed distance between two taxa in a cluster.
